To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the deep learning models still cannot recognize images that contain the following patterns: (1) images with multiple objects that are not related to each other; (2) images that have a large number of small objects; (3) images with multiple similar objects; (4) images that have objects with a large amount of background.

the deep learning model has difficulty with images that are (1) not well-defined in their category, (2) have a low-resolution, (3) contain a lot of noise, (4) have a small object, (5) are not well-aligned, (6) are not well-lit, (7) have a small size, (8) have a lot of background, and (9) have a lot in the background.

the failure cases in ImageNet can be categorized into three patterns: 1) the image has no object; 2) the object in the image is not the main object; and 3) the image is a close-up shot of a part of the object.

the current deep learning models still have difficulty in recognizing the images with the following characteristics: 1) low-resolution, 2) complex background, 3) small objects, 4) occlusion, 5) blur, 6) low-contrast.
the ImageNet database still needs to improve the quality of the images and annotations, and the deep learning community needs more efforts to improve the robustness of the deep learning models.

deep learning models are still vulnerable to various kinds of images, and it seems that they are not yet able to recognize images with complex backgrounds, images with multiple objects, images with occlusions or deformations, images with low resolution or blurry, or images with unusual poses.

the failure cases of recent deep learning model in ImageNet can be classified into three categories: the cases of misclassification, the cases of mislocalization, and the cases of misidentification.
the deep learning model is more sensitive to the color and shape of the object than to its size and texture.
